fluxsim init.description: Write a small FLUX bundle and its FLUID contract into a directory, so a first run needs nothing else checked out. With --contract and --profile, write a bundle for your own data instead: the contract, and a Simulation declared from the profile's published aggregates, with every number labelled in its parameter register (from the profile, from the contract, or assumed, with the reason). Each assumed number a profile statistic would answer names it, and the profile request for exactly those statistics is written inside the directory, as requests/assumptions.profile-request.yml. With --contract and no profile, write the profile request instead: the list of statistics and fact shares a profiler must measure for that contract, to run init again with. A profile with date pairs, calendars or exposure also gives the Simulation lifetimes, within entries, rates and exposure: docs/how-to/keep-dates-inside-their-parents-lifetime.md reads them. The directory must not exist yet, or must be empty: nothing is ever overwritten.

examples.note: write a project into a new directory
or into the current directory, if it is empty
no profile yet: write the profile request a profiler measures, then run again

fluxsim plan.description: Execute the whole pipeline once, in memory, and write down what it saw: inputDigest, the seed-tree paths it materialised, the per-emit seam digests, and each declared fidelity block as it compiled, every epsilon included. Writes plan.json and seed-paths.ndjson under the run directory, and stages the rows it generated there too, so that apply --run-id commits them instead of generating them again. A child table that a counts entry lays out comes out grouped by parent in row order, as a table loaded parent by parent does; a consumer that needs another order sorts it. The child's own key is laid out from the row index, so a number or date key in ascending order gives a parent's children consecutive keys, and a text or UUID key, permuted, does not.

fluxsim apply.description: Write every run artifact of a recorded plan: the population, the events, the emit streams and their seam attestations, the run digest and the receipt. With --run-id, commits what plan staged after checking the plan, the bundle and every staged file, and generates nothing; with no staged rows it executes the plan again. Refuses when the plan or the bundle has moved since the plan was recorded. A run whose bundle declares generator plugins, once committed, is kept as it stands: apply never asks the plugin for its rows again or writes the run directory over, and with --sink it delivers the run's files. A child table that a counts entry lays out comes out grouped by parent in row order, as a table loaded parent by parent does; a consumer that needs another order sorts it. The child's own key is laid out from the row index, so a number or date key in ascending order gives a parent's children consecutive keys, and a text or UUID key, permuted, does not.

examples.note: apply the plan recorded under that id (`plan` prints it)
write the first of four shares of that run (no receipt; a share is not a run)
apply the run whole and write every stream as Parquet

fluxsim run.description: Plan and apply in one call, then optionally verify, write every stream to a sink, and ship. Stops at the first stage that exits non-zero; the artifacts of every stage that did run are still returned under that stage's own key. When the run is already committed and its bundle declares generator plugins, the run is kept as it stands, the plugin is not asked again, and the rest of what was asked is done against it; a new sample needs a new run, for example another seed. With --verify and --profile the run is also scored against the pinned profile: each property the fidelity block declares, among them rankCorrelation and any property grouped by the bins of another column (groupByBins), is compared with it. Each counts entry of the bundle adds the rule lines counts:<relationship>.minChildren and counts:<relationship>.parentWhen to the child's rules, both enforced, and a profile that publishes the children per parent of a relationship adds a childrenPerParent row to the scorecard; a row of a relationship whose counts entry has given fails the run when it is outside the entry's tolerance.

examples.note: plan, apply, verify and ship in one command
plan and apply only
plan and apply at ten times the declared row counts (tables built from events stay as they are)
plan, apply and write every stream as Parquet
plan, apply and load every stream into a DuckDB table

fluxsim verify.description: Re-check an applied run on five independent legs: the run's own artifacts against its recorded digest, the golden regression, row conformance against the referenced contract, the RFC-04 enforcement vectors, and every declared fidelity check. One line per leg, with the flag that turns a `not checked` leg into a result. A run whose plan pins a profile is also scored against it, per property, table, dimension and overall, when the profile is passed with --profile. A bundle that declares consumer queries has every query counted on the run, the calibration queries apart from the held-out ones (--held-out), in the scorecard's queries dimension. Each counts entry of the bundle adds the rule lines counts:<relationship>.minChildren and counts:<relationship>.parentWhen to the child's rules, both enforced, and a profile that publishes the children per parent of a relationship adds a childrenPerParent row to the scorecard; a row of a relationship whose counts entry has given fails the stage when it is outside the entry's tolerance.

A bundle that declares consumer queries has them counted for the scorecard's queries dimension, as verify counts them.

fluxsim story.description: Tell the history of one row of a committed run: the rows that link to it and the rows it links to, through the relationships the run's contract declares, a few hops out, ordered by their first date or timestamp column. Each stream is checked against the receipt's outputDigest before it is read, and nothing is written. Every row of the expose that matches --key is the entity, and its rows come first. A first line says how many rows matched. Then one line per row: its date, its expose, its key, its hop (0 for the entity's own rows, n for a row reached after n relationships), the relationship it was reached by (- at hop 0), then column=value pairs, with control characters written out. With --json, a story is one JSON object per row, with hop and relationship, and no envelope; a refusal is the usual JSON envelope.

examples.note: the rows that link to customer 42 and the rows it links to, two hops out

fluxsim story --run-id de72fa4b22711c52 --emit store_returns \

fluxsim forecast make.description: Run the Simulation's spec.sweep as replicates, each seeded as the sweep seeds it and each taking the effect at the midpoint of its part of the response estimate's interval. For each forecast item, take the median of its value over the replicates and an interval around it, and register that, sealed and write-once, under the item's id and the pinned profile's digest. The same forecast again changes nothing; another forecast under that id is refused (FLX-7007), and the refusal says when the id belongs to another bundle.

fluxsim forecast score.description: Read the next state's profile and give a verdict to every forecast registered for the bundle, none skipped. The observation is the next state's cell for the forecast's query and segment; a withheld cell, or one that holds no records, leaves the forecast not scored, with the reason. Beside inside or outside the interval, each verdict holds the absolute error and the interval score, and the grade of each state's profile. A next state that is the pinned state is refused (FLX-7143). When forecasts.playback names a Playback that declares drift, the two states' histograms and the query cells the families read are compared with its metric (psi, kl or ks), each verdict records the largest value, and a statistic past the threshold marks the calibration stale; a cell withheld or with no records in either state is left out and listed. With onBreach fail the command then exits 1 (FLX-7146), after every verdict is written.

examples.note: score every forecast against the next state's cells
